title: How to look at a temple wall

steps.title: Locate the stone
steps.body: First identify the correct wall, face, column or doorway; a similar motif may occur elsewhere.

steps.title: Separate image from inscription
steps.body: Describe the depicted figures and actions before attempting to translate text.

steps.title: Notice carving technique
steps.body: Look at whether forms stand proud of the background or are cut into the stone; repairs and later recarving complicate the evidence.

steps.title: Identify a royal name cautiously
steps.body: A cartouche outlines a royal name, but a name can be reused or re-cut. A specific text requires a published reading.

steps.title: Compare a documented edition
steps.body: Use wall labels and numbered plates in a scholarly epigraphic edition; never infer ancient text solely from a modern summary.

caveats: This introduction is observational, not a lesson claiming to teach verified hieroglyph readings.
A later lesson will demonstrate actual signs only once photo, edition and transliteration have been aligned.
